questions.concept: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question: Which element is located in Group 18 of the periodic table and is known for its lack of chemical reactivity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Helium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Helium** is a chemical element and is part of **Group 18** (Noble Gases) in the **Periodic Table**.
 
• It is known for its **inertness** due to its full valence electron shell, making it highly stable and almost non-reactive under normal conditions.
 
• **Helium** has **two protons** and is represented by the symbol **He**.
 
• It is the **second-lightest** and **second-most abundant element** in the universe, following hydrogen.
 
• Helium is a **colorless, odorless, and tasteless gas** at room temperature and is widely used for applications requiring non-reactivity, such as in balloons, cryogenics, and as a protective gas in welding.
 
• Its **low boiling point** (-268.93°C) makes it useful in applications like cooling superconducting magnets in MRI machines.
 
• As a noble gas, helium has **no tendency to gain, lose, or share electrons**, which explains its lack of chemical reactivity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Oxygen**__

 __
 
• **Oxygen** is a highly reactive element and belongs to **Group 16** of the periodic table, also known as the chalcogens.
 
• It is essential for **respiration** in living organisms and is a part of the Earth's atmosphere (~21%).
 
• Oxygen readily forms compounds, such as water (H₂O), due to its high electronegativity.
 
• It is not inert and reacts with many elements and compounds.
 
 
 
• ** Chlorine**__
 __
 
• **Chlorine** is a highly reactive halogen belonging to **Group 17** of the periodic table.
 
• It is widely used as a **disinfectant** and in the production of **plastics** like PVC (polyvinyl chloride).
 
• Chlorine forms compounds such as sodium chloride (common salt) and is not chemically inert.
 
 
 
• ** Fluorine**__
 
 
• **Fluorine** is the most reactive element in the periodic table and belongs to **Group 17** (halogens).
 
• It has a high electronegativity, which makes it highly reactive with most elements, including some noble gases under specific conditions.
 
• Fluorine compounds, such as fluoride, are widely used in toothpaste and water fluoridation to prevent dental cavities.

questions.concept: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question: The elements that are liquid at room temperature (25°C) are:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**bromine and mercury**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bromine (Br)** and **mercury (Hg)** are the only two elements that are liquid at room temperature (25ºC).
 
• **Bromine** is a reddish-brown liquid and is the only non-metallic element that is liquid at room temperature.
 
• **Mercury** is a silvery liquid metal, known for its unique property of being liquid at room temperature.
 
• Both elements have significant industrial and scientific applications due to their unique physical properties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Melting and Boiling Points:** Bromine melts at -7.2°C and boils at 58.8°C, while mercury melts at -38.83°C and boils at 356.7°C.
 
• **Density:** Bromine has a density of 3.1028 g/cm³, and mercury has a density of 13.534 g/cm³, making it one of the densest liquids.
 
• **Toxicity:** Both bromine and mercury are toxic and require careful handling. Mercury exposure can lead to mercury poisoning, while bromine can cause burns and respiratory issues.
 
• **Uses of Bromine:** Bromine is used in flame retardants, water purification, and as a reactant in organic synthesis.
 
• **Uses of Mercury:** Mercury is used in thermometers, barometers, fluorescent lamps, and amalgams for dental fillings, though its use has decreased due to toxicity concerns.

questions.question: What chemical element does ‘H’ stand for in the science periodic table?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydrogen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chemical symbols **are the **abbreviations **used in **chemistry for chemical elements**, **functional groups, **and **chemical compounds**.
 
• **Element symbols **for **chemical elements **normally consist of **one or two letters **from the **Latin alphabet **and are written with the **first letter capitalised**.
 
• **A chemical symbol **is a **one- or two-letter **designation of **an element**.
 
• **A chemical symbol **is a **one- or two-letter designation **of **an element**.
 
• Some examples of **chemical symbols **are **O for oxygen**, **Zn for zinc**, **H for hydrogen, **and **Fe for iron**. 
 
• **The first letter **of **a symbol **is **always capitalized**. If the **symbol contains two letters**, **the second letter **is **lowercase**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Helium **is donated by **He**.
 
• **Holmium **is donated by **Ho**.
 
• **Mercury **is donated by **Hg**.

questions.question: What chemical element does 'N' stand for in the periodic table?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Nitrogen**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Nitrogen's symbol is N. Nitrogen is number 7 on the periodic table and has 2 core electrons and 5 valence electrons. 
 
• Nitrogen's electron configuration is 1s2 2s2 2p3. Nitrogen, N, is a colorless, odorless, gaseous element that is about four-fifths of the volume of the atmosphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Neptunium is a chemical element with the symbol Np and atomic number 93. A radioactive actinide metal, neptunium is the first transuranic element. Its position in the periodic table is just after uranium, named after the planet Uranus. A neptunium atom has 93 protons and 93 electrons, of which seven are valence electrons. 
 
• Neon (Ne), a chemical element, inert gas of Group 18 (noble gases) of the periodic table, used in electric signs and fluorescent lamps.
 
• Neodymium is a chemical element with the symbol Nd and atomic number 60. It is the fourth member of the lanthanide series.

questions.question: What is the atomic number of sulphur?
questions.solution:
The atomic number of Sulphur is __**16**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sulphur is a **pale yellow nonmetallic element** occurring widely in nature in several free, allotropic, and crystal forms.
 
• Its **atomic mass** is **32**.
 
• Historically and in literature sulfur is also called** brimstone** which means** "burning stone"**.
 
• When burned, sulfur melts into a blood-red liquid and emits a blue flame.
 
• It melts at** 115.21 °C (239.38 °F)**, boils at **444.6 °C (832.3 °F),** and sublimates easily.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The first periodic table to become generally accepted was that of the **Russian chemist Dmitri Mendeleev in 1869.**
 
• On **17 February 1869 (1 March 1869 in the Gregorian calendar), Mendeleev** began arranging the elements and comparing them by their **atomic weights**.
 
• In **1875**, the** French chemist Paul-Émile Lecoq de Boisbaudran** discovered a new element in a sample of the mineral sphalerite and named it** Gallium**.
 
• Atoms with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons are called** isotopes**.
 
• The 83 elements that have survived the formation of the Earth are called** primordial**. All 24 known artificial elements are radioactive.

questions.concept: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question: What is the atomic number of Carbon as per Mendeleev's Periodic Table?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The atomic number of carbon is 6.**
 
• Carbon is a chemical element with the** atomic number 6 and the symbol C.**
 
• It is a **nonmetallic element** that can bond with itself and other elements to form a wide variety of compounds.
 
• Carbon is **essential for life on Earth** as it is a** key component of organic compounds, which make up living organisms.**
 
• It exists in** several forms, including diamond, graphite, and amorphous carbon.**
 
• Carbon-based fuels like coal, oil, and natural gas are the primary source of energy for many modern technologies but their **combustion releases carbon dioxide (CO2) into the atmosphere.**
 
• **CO2 is a greenhouse gas** that contributes to climate change.
 
• It is** also used in the form of activated carbon in water purification, air filters, and gas masks.**
 
• **Carbon is abundant in the Earth's crust and atmosphere.**
 
• **Carbon **plays a crucial role in many aspects of our lives, but its impact on the environment requires careful consideration and management.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0eb8d09360b87ae816aa01e02dd8c8750506f883689c1355a89db72d48cde4e3.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Atomic Number:**

 
 
• The atomic number is the** number of protons in the nucleus of an atom.**
 
• It is a** fundamental property of an element **and determines its **identity of the element.**
 
• Atoms of the same element have the same atomic number.
 
• The **atomic number **is represented by the **symbol "Z".**
 
• In a neutral atom, the** atomic number** also equals the **number of electrons in the atom.**
 
• The atomic number is used to organize elements in the** periodic table of elements.**
 
• Elements are arranged in order o**f increasing atomic number in the periodic table.**
 
• The** atomic number **can be used to determine the** number of neutrons in an atom, as well as other properties of the atom.**

questions.question: What is the atomic number of hydrogen in the Mendeleev's periodic table?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Option 1**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• ** In Mendeleev's periodic table**,** hydrogen **was given a unique position outside the main group elements, because its properties did not fit well into any of the groups.
 
• Therefore, it was not assigned an atomic number in Mendeleev's original periodic table. However, in the **modern periodic table,** hydrogen is placed in **Group 1** (the alkali metals) and has an atomic number of **1**.

questions.question: An image of which of the following elements is shown by the map of Cyprus from which the element got its name?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Copper**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The element **Copper** is symbolized by the map of Cyprus.
 
• The name **Copper** is derived from the Latin word *Cyprium*, meaning "metal of Cyprus."
 
• In ancient times, Cyprus was a major source of copper, which was extensively mined and traded.
 
• Copper is a highly conductive metal used in electrical wiring, plumbing, and various other applications.
 
• It is also an essential trace element necessary for the survival of all living organisms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Copper** has the chemical symbol **Cu** and atomic number 29.
 
• It is known for its reddish-orange color and high thermal and electrical conductivity.
 
• Copper has been used by humans for at least 10,000 years, with evidence of its use dating back to ancient civilizations.
 
• The element is found in various ores, including chalcopyrite, bornite, and malachite.
 
• Modern-day applications of copper include electrical equipment, construction materials, and industrial machinery.
